line: Technical Program Manager, Extensibility / Technical Program Manager, Extensibility Platform / Technical Program Manager, Money-as-a-Service (the titles)
why: The title rule's core tier listed "Technical Program Manager" (v1.0.0 to v1.1.0-d), so these titles matched as PM roles. Aravind's hand verdict on all three: not relevant, program delivery only, partnering with or influencing PMs rather than owning product direction (FILTER.md §1 TPM rule). Under v1.1.0-a to v1.1.0-d this match changed 3 decisions against the hand verdicts (kept instead of rejected). Fixed in v1.1.0-e: TPM titles moved to the adjacent tier.

line: Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands.
why: In both rows it appears only in Airbnb's pay boilerplate (corpus count: 172 of 203 Airbnb postings). It is not a filter word in any version, so it changed no decision. It would be a false friend if it were added to the topic terms.

line: Stripe's company intro, e.g. "... use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities."
why: v1.1.0-b drops topic words that appear only in lines shared by at least 20% of a board's postings, but it matches exact lines only. 159 Stripe postings still count "payments" that appears only in a reworded company intro (FILTER.md §9, v1.1.0-b). No judged audit row's outcome depended on it.
